## Why This Is Asked
Explores real-world cross-architecture provenance enforcement and per-tenant key management in CNF environments.

## Key Concepts
- Architecture-aware image provenance
- Per-tenant KMS signing keys
- SPDX SBOM with architecture metadata
- OPA Gatekeeper policy for imagePull enforcement
- Namespace-scoped validation tests

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sArchConstraint
spec:
 match:
   kinds:
   - Pod
 parameters:
   allowedArchitectures: ['amd64', 'arm64']
```

```yaml
# test Deployment (arm64 image on amd64 node should be rejected)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test-arm64-deployment
  namespace: test-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-arm64
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-arm64
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/arch: amd64
      containers:
      - name: test-container
        image: example.com/app:arm64-latest
        imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical runtime network security for multi-tenant CNF gateways, requiring hands-on knowledge of Cilium, Kubernetes NetworkPolicies, DNS controls, and observability in a distributed environment.

## Key Concepts
- CiliumNetworkPolicy
- NetworkPolicy basics
- tenantID labeling
- per-tenant DNS allowlists
- observability with cilium policy trace

## Code Example
```yaml
# CiliumNetworkPolicy isolating by tenantID
apiVersion: "cilium.io/v2"
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-isolation
  namespace: cnf-gws
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenantID: "tA"
  ingress:
  - from:
    - sourceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          tenantID: "tA"
  egress:
  - toEndpoints:
    - matchLabels:
        tenantID: "tA"
```
```yaml
# Kubernetes NetworkPolicy for per-tenant gateway
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-tenant-gateway
  namespace: cnf-gws
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      tenantID: "tA"
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.1.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical policy design and enforcement in a real multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on OSS Gatekeeper usage, per-namespace configuration, and testability.

Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy referencing namespace ConfigMap values
- Per-tenant overrides via Namespace annotations/config
- Lightweight tests to verify enforcement
- Minimal YAML scaffolding for quick rollout checks

Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: defines RateLimitTemplate for K8sRateLimit
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sratelimittemplate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRateLimit
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sratelimit
      # Pseudocode: reads per-namespace cnf.rate-limit and enforces a per-minute cap
      defaultRate := 100
      rateLimitPerMin := data.rateLimitPerMin
      # implementation would map namespace to rate and count requests
      # returns deny if burst exceeds rate
```

```yaml
# Constraint: per-tenant rate limit value
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sRateLimit
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rate-limit
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      kinds: ["Namespace"]
  parameters:
    rateLimitPerMin: 200
    targetPath: "/gateway"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest overriding default rate for tenant-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    cnf.rate-limit: "200"  # override default 100/min
```

```yaml
# Simple test pod to generate burst traffic for validation
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: rate-limit-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  containers:
  - name: curl
    image: curlimages/curl:7.85.0
    command: ["sh", "-c", "for i in {1..150}; do curl -s http://gateway-service/gateway || true; done"]
```

Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for token-bucket bursts and global vs tenant-specific ceilings?
- What are trade-offs of storing counters in-memory vs external stores for scale?

kind: TenantFailoverPolicy

```go
// Controller reconciliation logic (simplified)
func (r *TenantFailoverPolicyReconciler) Reconcile(ctx context.Context, req ctrl.Request) error {
    policy := &cnfv1.TenantFailoverPolicy{}
    if err := r.Get(ctx, req.NamespacedName, policy); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    // Poll control-plane health
    healthy := r.checkControlPlaneHealth(policy.Spec.Tenant)

    if !healthy {
        policy.Status.FailureCount++
        if policy.Status.FailureCount >= policy.Spec.UnhealthyThreshold {
            return r.executeFailover(policy)
        }
    } else {
        policy.Status.FailureCount = 0
    }
    return nil
}

func (r *TenantFailoverPolicyReconciler) executeFailover(policy *cnfv1.TenantFailoverPolicy) error {
    // Update Ingress to point to standby
    ingress := &networkingv1.Ingress{}
    r.Get(ctx, types.NamespacedName{Name: "gateway-ingress", Namespace: policy.Spec.Tenant}, ingress)
    ingress.Spec.Default.Backend.Service.Name = policy.Spec.StandbyGateway
    r.Update(ctx, ingress)

    // Update SPIRE TLS identity binding
    return r.updateSPIREEntry(policy)
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

```go
// Pseudocode for version negotiation
func negotiate(upstreamVersions []string, tenantID string) string {
    tenantVersions := registry.GetVersions(tenantID)
    allowed := intersect(upstreamVersions, tenantVersions)
    if len(allowed) == 0 {
        return DEFAULT_VERSION
    }
    return highestVersion(allowed)
}
```

## Implementation Highlights

- Extract X-TENANT-ID header in sidecar middleware
- Query central registry for tenant capabilities
- Compute intersection with upstream supported versions
- Select highest compatible version using semver comparison
- Store result in tenant-scoped cache with configurable TTL
- Return 406 if negotiation fails and no default is configured
- Emit histogram metrics for negotiation latency and cache hit rates

  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
      tenant: a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        tenant: a
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: registry.example.com/cnf/gateway:latest
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 5m }
      - setWeight: 100
      analysis:
        templates:
        - templateName: canary-metrics
        metrics:
        - name: latency
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.001 * 0.15
        - name: error-rate
          interval: 30s
          successCondition: result < 0.005

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: canary-metrics
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: latency
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))
  - name: error-rate
    provider:
      prometheus:
        url: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status!~"2.."}[5m]))
